methodology: 10,000-run Monte Carlo simulation over full 14-week Sleeper schedule & 6-team playoff bracket with official tiebreakers.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Defending champion brings elite veteran floor and balanced scoring depth
fluctuationNarrative.trend: Up +0.7 wins after rookie draft consolidation
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: McBride and a deep veteran running back stable keep the weekly projection at 122+ points. The model projects them to secure a first-round bye in 42.1% of simulations.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Age profile ranks 12th; late-season veteran wear could introduce variance in playoff rounds.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Premier running back trio gives huge weekly ceiling despite concentrated roster
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Gibbs, Jeanty, and Taylor give 2 Dagos the best RB unit in the league. When all three play, win probability against average opponents jumps to 71%.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: QB and WR rooms rank in the bottom tier, making comebacks difficult if trailing early.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: High-powered core carries top-two upside, but bench cushion is razor-thin
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Justin Jefferson, Brock Bowers, and Lamar Jackson produce explosive single-week scoring spikes, resulting in a 92% playoff rate across 10,000 simulations.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Depth ranks 10th league-wide. If injuries hit during Weeks 9-11 bye clusters, win rate drops by 24%.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Youngest roster in the league with elite pick capital; QB bottleneck holds back 2026
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Breece Hall and Jeremiyah Love supply an outstanding RB foundation. However, quarterback uncertainty and youth concentration keep the 2026 projection at 4.9 wins.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Low immediate win-now scoring; simulator places them in seeds 9–12 in 74% of runs.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: High-upside youth movement primed for rapid ascent as young receivers mature
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Nabers and McMillan supply dynamic WR upside. The simulator shows a wide range of outcomes (3 to 9 wins), reflecting the youth and developmental volatility.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: RB room ranks 12th in starter scoring, making weekly floor vulnerable against power rushing teams.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Rebuild has an exciting new anchor, but full weekly offense remains uphill
fluctuationNarrative.trend: Up +0.8 wins after drafting Carnell Tate
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Drafting Carnell Tate at 1.03 adds a marquee piece to the rebuild. The redraft lineup still ranks 12th, keeping playoff probability at 14.8%.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Severe RB depth shortage limits weekly scoring floor across all 14 matchups.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Elite backfield power balanced by league's most volatile receiver corps
fluctuationNarrative.trend: Down -0.8 wins due to WR room uncertainty
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Achane, Hampton, and McCaffrey form a dominant RB room that wins weeks outright, but the bottom-ranked WR room creates volatility against top-scoring opponents.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: With three FLEX spots, any missed games from top RBs drastically reduces lineup efficiency.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Balanced middle-class profile without glaring weaknesses or elite separation
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: CeeDee Lamb and A.J. Brown supply WR ceiling, while tight end remains the limiting factor. The simulator projects a tight 5th–8th seed outcome in 64% of runs.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Lack of high-end RB depth leaves little room for scoring explosions against top-3 contenders.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Superstar wideouts provide explosive spikes alongside a thinner baseline
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Ja'Marr Chase and Garrett Wilson create massive weekly variance. In high-scoring shootout weeks, Gridiron Gorilla wins 68% of simulated games.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Low-ranked tight end and depth value limit floor in standard weekly grinds.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Deepest roster in the league provides supreme injury insulation
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Bijan Robinson and Amon-Ra St. Brown pair with the No. 2 QB room. Having top-ranked depth means substitute starters suffer almost no degradation during bye weeks.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: WR depth is concentrated in middle tiers; needs one receiver to hit high-end WR1 ceiling in playoff weeks.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Retooling roster with solid depth building toward next consolidation window
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Terry Tate's Pain Train has the 5th ranked depth, but lacks the elite top-5 difference makers needed to reliably beat the top 3 contenders in the simulation.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Low starting lineup ceiling results in a projected 32% playoff rate.

fluctuationNarrative.headline: Elite lineup floor creates the league's highest regular season ceiling
fluctuationNarrative.analysis: Red Zone Renegades boasts the No. 1 redraft starting lineup. Even with zero 2027 firsts, their weekly scoring consistency insulates them from major matchup variance across 14 weeks.
fluctuationNarrative.keyRisk: Tight end room lacks top-tier insurance; an injury to starter would force backup FLEX adjustments.
